newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Floods reach western Ukraine, PM to visit area.
newsitem.headline: Floods reach western Ukraine, PM to visit area.

text.p: Floods caused by heavy rains have hit Lviv region in western Ukraine, leaving 50 villages and small towns partly under water, the local authority said on Tuesday.

"Heavy rains last weekend caused the water levels in some rivers to rise between three and 3.5 metres (10 to 12 feet)," a spokesman for Lviv regional administration said, naming the Dnestr, Striy and Yablonka rivers.

"More than 1,700 houses in 50 villages and small towns were affected by the waters, about 800 people were evacuated," said spokesman Viktor Kobzarenko, contacted by telephone in Lviv, some 500 km (300 miles) west of Kiev.
He said no deaths had been reported during the floods.
Kobzarenko said newly-appointed Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko was due to visit the area on Wednesday.
The UNIAN news agency said Pustovoitenko on Tuesday allocated two million hryvnias ($1.1 million) from government funds to repair the flood damage.

Some of central Europe's worst floods this century, which have claimed over 100 lives in Poland and the Czech Republic this month, reached eastern Germany last week as the Oder burst through dikes in three places.
An agriculture official from Lviv administration said 44,000 hectares (108,000 acres) of grain, or about 10 percent of the total sown area in the Lviv region had been affected.
